maritime.title: NERAI Maritime Weekly
events: US–Iran tanker war escalates: Sidr struck, 2 Filipino sailors killed, US destroys 3 Iranian tankers
Houthi offensive toward Bab al-Mandeb kills 129, pushes Bab el-Mandeb flow to SEVERE
Taiwan Strait 4-week disruption probability surges 10 points to 54% — highest in corpus
Japanese tanker giant warns Hormuz disruptions could drag into 2027 as commercial avoidance deepens
maritime.summary: The week was dominated by two interlocking crises that are now compounding each other: the US–Iran conflict has driven Strait of Hormuz oil transit to a SEVERE -92.9% versus baseline, while a simultaneous Houthi offensive toward Bab al-Mandeb has pushed that chokepoint into SEVERE territory as well (-33.3% vs baseline). Four corridors are deteriorating on the model and in the water simultaneously, creating a vessel and port-capacity squeeze that transforms rerouting from a cost into a structural constraint. The Taiwan Strait forward disruption probability rose 10.2 points to 54% over four weeks, adding a third, independent axis of risk that markets have not yet fully priced.

sanctions.title: NERAI Sanctions Weekly
events: US Treasury Designates Turkish Bank and Two Subsidiaries Over Iran Links
Iran Announces Imminent New Gulf Restricted Zone; Anti-Destroyer Missile Fired at US Vessel
UK Set to Announce Trade Ban on Israeli Settlement Goods on Tuesday
EU Forces Board Sixth Suspected Russian Shadow-Fleet Tanker
US Calls for All-Out UN Arms Embargo on Sudan as External Networks Fuel War
sanctions.summary: The week's dominant sanctions theme was US escalation against Iran's financial infrastructure, centred on the designation of a Turkish bank and two subsidiaries for allegedly processing Iranian funds through the Türkiye corridor. Separately, Iran announced plans for a new Gulf restricted zone and deployed an anti-destroyer missile against a US vessel, sharply lifting oil-price risk. The UK moved toward a trade ban on Israeli settlement goods, while diplomatic pressure mounted—without result—for a UN arms embargo on Sudan.
